# Use the agent SDK you already know

Create the search capabilities you need and add them to your SDK's normal tool
collection:

```python
from serpapi_search_tools import hotels_search, maps_search, web_search

tools = [web_search(), maps_search(), hotels_search()]
```

The package prepares the tool name, description, inputs, validation, and
SerpApi request. You continue to choose the model and run the agent through
your SDK as usual.

## Installation choices

If your agent SDK is already installed, add only the base package:

```bash
pip install serpapi-search-tools
```

If you want this package to install a compatible SDK dependency too, use its
extra. For example:

```bash
pip install "serpapi-search-tools[openai-agents]"
```

Replace `openai-agents` with the extra in the table below.

## Supported SDKs

| SDK | Extra / explicit provider | Supported range | Complete example |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| OpenAI Agents SDK | `openai-agents` | `openai-agents >=0.18.3,<1` | [OpenAI Agents](../sdk-examples/openai_agents.html) |
| Pydantic AI | `pydantic-ai` | `pydantic-ai >=1.30.1,<3` | [Pydantic AI](../sdk-examples/pydantic_ai.html) |
| LangChain | `langchain` | `langchain >=1.3.11,<2` | [LangChain](../sdk-examples/langchain.html) |
| LangGraph | `langgraph` | `langgraph >=1.2.6,<2` | [LangGraph](../sdk-examples/langgraph.html) |
| CrewAI | `crewai` | `crewai >=1.6.1,<2` | [CrewAI](../sdk-examples/crewai.html) |
| LlamaIndex | `llamaindex` | core `>=0.14.22,<0.15` | [LlamaIndex](../sdk-examples/llamaindex.html) |
| Claude Agent SDK | `claude-agent-sdk` | `claude-agent-sdk >=0.2.108,<1` | [Claude Agent SDK](../sdk-examples/claude_agent_sdk.html) |
| Microsoft Agent Framework | `microsoft-agent-framework` | `agent-framework-openai >=1.10.1,<2` | [Microsoft Agent Framework](../sdk-examples/microsoft_agent_framework.html) |
| AutoGen | `autogen` | AgentChat `>=0.7.5,<0.8` | [AutoGen](../sdk-examples/autogen.html) |
| Haystack | `haystack` | `haystack-ai >=2.30.2,<4` | [Haystack](../sdk-examples/haystack.html) |
| Agno | `agno` | `agno >=2.6.19,<3` | [Agno](../sdk-examples/agno.html) |
| smolagents | `smolagents` | `smolagents >=1.26,<2` | [smolagents](../sdk-examples/smolagents.html) |
| Google ADK | `google-adk` | `google-adk >=2.3,<3` | [Google ADK](../sdk-examples/google_adk.html) |
| Semantic Kernel | `semantic-kernel` | `semantic-kernel >=1.36,<2` | [Semantic Kernel](../sdk-examples/semantic_kernel.html) |

You only need dependencies for the SDKs you use. The base install remains small
and also supports direct Python calls.

Microsoft Agent Framework is the successor recommended by Microsoft for new
AutoGen and Semantic Kernel agent applications. The AutoGen and Semantic Kernel
rows remain available for projects that have not migrated.

## Automatic detection is the normal path

When one supported SDK is installed, omit `provider`:

```python
from serpapi_search_tools import web_search

tool = web_search()
```

If multiple supported SDK families are installed, automatic detection raises
an error rather than selecting by import order. Pass the table's provider value
explicitly:

```python
from serpapi_search_tools import web_search

tool = web_search(provider="openai-agents")
```

Use the same explicit provider for every tool in one agent.
LangGraph and LangChain count as one adapter family.

## No supported SDK installed

Automatic detection falls back to a normal callable. You can request that form
directly with `provider="function"` for scripts, tests, or an unlisted agent
framework. See [Support another agent SDK](configuration.html#support-another-agent-sdk).

## Compatibility notes

The package supports Python 3.10 through 3.14. Fresh test environments build
the wheel and resolve every SDK extra independently within its declared range.
SDK extras declare only the packages needed to construct that SDK's SerpApi
tool. They do not select an OpenAI, Anthropic, or other model integration for
your application, and they do not pin shared transitive dependencies such as
Pydantic. Complete examples install their chosen model backend explicitly.

CrewAI is supported on Python 3.10 through 3.13. Install Google ADK in its own
environment because its extension dependencies can conflict with the supported
LangChain and LangGraph branches. Microsoft Agent Framework is compatible with
the `frameworks` bundle's OpenAI dependency branch. The `frameworks`
convenience extra is for compatible repository integration tests; applications
should normally install one SDK extra so its resolver can select mutually
compatible transitive dependencies.

If you want to add SDK support to the package itself, see
[Contributing](contributing.html).
